formation.title: The North Sea Empire Reborn
formation.text:
The dream of Cnut the Great lives again. Where once a single king united the thrones of England, Denmark, and Norway through force of arms and force of personality, we have surpassed even that legendary achievement. The North Sea, that vast grey expanse that separates lesser nations, is now our inner lake, our highway, our lifeblood.

But an empire held together by water faces a fundamental question that Cnut himself never answered: what kind of power shall we be? The sea that unites us also defines us. We can embrace that identity fully, becoming the supreme maritime power of the age, our fleets unchallenged from the Faeroes to the Skagerrak. Or we can use the sea merely as the connective tissue of something greater: a unified crown that governs three nations as one, blending Anglo-Saxon law with Norse custom into a new imperial tradition.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The whale road is our empire

modifiers.name: The Whale Road
modifiers.text: The sea is not a barrier but a highway. Our fleets bind three kingdoms into one, and the whale road carries our merchants, our warriors, and our laws to every shore of the northern world.

options.text: One crown, three kingdoms, one law

modifiers.name: Crown of Three Kingdoms
modifiers.text: England, Denmark, and Norway answer to a single crown. What Cnut forged through conquest, we shall sustain through law and governance, weaving three peoples into one imperium.

advances.name: Huscarl Tradition
advances.text: The institution of the huscarls, professional household warriors modeled on the legendary Jomsvikings, provides the North Sea Empire with an elite standing infantry force.

advances.name: The Danegeld System
advances.text: Originally tribute paid to Viking raiders, the Danegeld has been transformed into a sophisticated land tax administered through the Anglo-Saxon shire system.

event.title: The Danegeld Perfected
event.text:
What began as tribute extorted from terrified Anglo-Saxon kings has become the most efficient tax system in northern Europe. The Danegeld, once a shameful payment to buy off Viking raiders, is now a sophisticated land tax, assessed by hide and collected by royal reeves across every shire. No other kingdom can match the thoroughness of our fiscal administration.

The question before us is how to direct this extraordinary revenue stream. We can tighten the collection apparatus further, ensuring that every last penny flows to the royal treasury and strengthening crown control over distant provinces. Or we can redirect a portion of this wealth into commercial infrastructure, reinvesting the Danegeld into the trade networks that make our empire prosperous.

modifiers.name: Danegeld Extraction
modifiers.text: A perfected system of land taxation ensures every hide in the realm contributes to the royal treasury.

modifiers.name: Danegeld Reinvestment
modifiers.text: Tax revenues are channeled back into commercial infrastructure, enriching the realm through trade.

advances.name: The Dreki Warship
advances.text: The dragon ship, the dreaded dreki, is the supreme expression of Norse naval engineering: fast, seaworthy, and terrifying to behold.

advances.name: Norse Trade Routes
advances.text: Viking-era trade networks spanning from Byzantium to Vinland provide the foundation for North Sea commerce, carried in the broad-beamed knarr.

advances.name: Thingstead Tradition
advances.text: The Norse Thing, an assembly of free men for lawmaking and dispute resolution, is institutionalized as a permanent governing body.

advances.name: Skaldic Heritage
advances.text: The rich tradition of Norse skaldic poetry, runestone carving, and oral history preserves and celebrates the empire's cultural identity.

advances.name: Leidang Origins
advances.text: The ancient Scandinavian naval levy system, requiring each coastal district to provide a ship and crew, forms the backbone of the empire's military reserves.

advances.name: The Snekkja Fleet
advances.text: Fast, agile longships known as snekkjas form the backbone of the empire's patrol and raiding fleet, outpacing any vessel on the open sea.

advances.name: Leidang Reform
advances.text: The old leidang system is reformed to produce the Thingmannalid: a standing retinue of professional soldiers funded by permanent taxation.

event.title: The Leidang Reforged
event.text:
The ancient leidang system, the naval levy that once mustered the fleets of Scandinavia, has been reformed for a new age. Under the old system, each coastal district was obligated to provide one ship and crew for seasonal expeditions. Now we have systematized and expanded this obligation across the entire North Sea Empire, from the fjords of Norway to the estuaries of eastern England.

Every skipreide and every shire along our vast coastline now contributes to a standing naval reserve. When the empire calls, hundreds of ships can be mustered within weeks. The sea that others fear is our fortress wall.

options.text: The North Sea shall know our keels

modifiers.name: The Leidang Reforged
modifiers.text: A reformed naval levy system provides rapid mobilization of fleets from every coastal district of the empire.

advances.name: Jelling Legacy
advances.text: The great runestones at Jelling, erected by Harald Bluetooth to mark Denmark's conversion to Christianity, symbolize the empire's capacity to bridge pagan and Christian traditions.

advances.name: Longship Yards Tradition
advances.text: Specialized shipbuilding facilities using the distinctive Norse clinker construction technique produce vessels of unmatched seaworthiness.

advances.name: North Sea Trade League
advances.text: A formalized network of trading partnerships across the North Sea, building on centuries of Viking commercial enterprise.

advances.name: Runestone Legacy
advances.text: The tradition of raising carved runestones to commemorate great deeds and preserve knowledge represents a unique form of public literacy and cultural memory.

advances.name: The Witan Council
advances.text: The Anglo-Saxon Witenagemot, the assembly of wise men, is blended with Norse Thing traditions to create a powerful advisory council for the crown.

advances.name: The Busse Warship
advances.text: The busse is a large, heavily-built warship evolved from the merchant knarr, capable of carrying both troops and heavy armament across the open North Sea.

advances.name: The Great Thing
advances.text: An empire-wide assembly brings together representatives from every corner of the North Sea realm, establishing precedents for cross-cultural governance.

event.title: The Great Heathen Thing
event.text:
In the ancient Norse tradition, the Thing was where free men gathered to settle disputes, proclaim laws, and hold their rulers accountable. Now, representatives from every corner of the North Sea Empire (English earls and Danish jarls, Norwegian lagmen and Scottish thanes) have gathered in the greatest assembly our world has ever seen.

This is more than a legal proceeding. It is the moment when three distinct peoples begin to see themselves as one. The laws proclaimed today will be written in three languages and enforced from Trondheim to Canterbury. What the sword began, the law will complete.

options.text: Let the law bind what the sword forged

modifiers.name: Legacy of the Great Thing
modifiers.text: The precedent of the Great Assembly has established a tradition of inclusive governance across the empire's diverse peoples.

advances.name: Cod and Stockfish Trade
advances.text: The processing and export of dried cod and stockfish becomes a cornerstone of North Sea commerce, feeding Europe while enriching the empire.

advances.name: Stave Church Architecture
advances.text: The distinctive Norse stave churches, with their dragon-headed gables and intricate woodcarvings, represent the unique fusion of Christian faith with Viking artistic tradition.

advances.name: Hird Discipline
advances.text: The royal hird, the professional military retinue of the Norse kings, develops rigorous training standards that raise the quality of the empire's standing forces.

advances.name: Naval Prowess
advances.text: Generations of seafaring experience culminate in a naval doctrine that combines Norse seamanship with advanced tactical coordination.

advances.name: Shire Integration
advances.text: The Anglo-Saxon shire system of local governance is extended across the empire, providing uniform administration from the Scottish highlands to the Norwegian fjords.

advances.name: North Sea Frigate
advances.text: Purpose-built frigates optimized for the rough waters of the North Sea and Atlantic, combining speed with the firepower needed to patrol vast maritime territories.

advances.name: Confessional Unity
advances.text: The North Sea Empire's tradition of bridging pagan and Christian, Catholic and Protestant, creates an unusual tolerance for religious diversity.

advances.name: Reformed Leidang
advances.text:
The medieval naval levy system is modernized into a comprehensive military obligation, producing both sailors for the fleet and soldiers for the army.

Available in: Hirdstova

advances.name: Wool and Cloth Trade
advances.text:
English wool and Scandinavian dyeing techniques combine to produce cloth that rivals the finest Flemish textiles.

Available in: Longship Yards

advances.name: Crown Law Reform
advances.text: A unified legal code draws from both Anglo-Saxon common law and Scandinavian legal traditions, strengthening royal authority across the empire.

advances.name: Hanseatic Rivalry
advances.text:
Competition with the Hanseatic League drives the North Sea Empire to develop its own merchant networks and trade infrastructure.

Available in: Danelaw Mint

advances.name: Fortress Harbors
advances.text: Key coastal ports are fortified with defensive works that protect both the fleet and the trade routes that sustain the empire.

advances.name: Rate of the Line
advances.text: The construction of massive ships of the line marks the North Sea Empire's emergence as a first-rate naval power, capable of projecting force across the Atlantic.

event.title: Mastery of the North Sea
event.text:
The launching of our great ships of the line marks the culmination of centuries of naval tradition. From the dragon-prowed longships that first terrorized the coasts of Europe to these towering floating fortresses bristling with cannon, the evolution of North Sea naval power has been relentless.

No fleet in the world can challenge our command of the northern waters. The approaches to every major port from Bergen to London lie under our guns. The herring fleets sail unmolested. The trade convoys arrive without interruption. The North Sea Empire is, at last, precisely what its name always promised: an empire of the sea.

options.text: We are masters of the northern deep

modifiers.name: Mastery of the North Sea
modifiers.text: Unchallenged naval supremacy over the northern waters, sustained by the most powerful battle fleet in the region.

advances.name: Absolute Thalassocracy
advances.text: The North Sea Empire's naval supremacy becomes total: no fleet dares challenge our warships, and every trade route in the northern waters operates under our protection.

advances.name: Navigation Acts
advances.text: Legislation requiring that trade with the empire be carried in empire-flagged vessels, securing the merchant marine's dominance over North Sea commerce.

advances.name: Cultural Convergence
advances.text: Centuries of shared governance have begun to forge a new identity from the old divisions: not quite Norse, not quite English, but something unprecedented.

advances.name: Imperial Navy Reform
advances.text: A comprehensive reorganization of the fleet introduces standardized ship designs, professional officer training, and centralized naval command.

advances.name: Colonial Mandate
advances.text: The North Sea Empire's maritime reach extends beyond European waters, establishing colonies and trading posts across the Atlantic.

advances.name: Constitutional Assembly
advances.text: A permanent legislative body representing all three kingdoms provides constitutional governance while preserving the unity of the crown.

advances.name: Nordhavskorvet
advances.text: Fast, modern corvettes designed for patrol and enforcement across the vast maritime territories of the North Sea Empire.

advances.name: Industrial Shipyards
advances.text:
Steam-powered machinery and iron construction techniques transform the empire's shipyards, enabling the rapid production of modern warships.

Available in: Longship Yards

advances.name: North Sea Enlightenment
advances.text: A flowering of scholarship and scientific inquiry across the empire, building on the combined intellectual traditions of Scandinavia and Britain.

advances.name: Maritime Insurance
advances.text: Formalized systems of maritime insurance reduce the financial risk of North Sea trade, encouraging greater commercial investment and longer voyages.

advances.name: Modern Navy Doctrine
advances.text: A comprehensive naval doctrine incorporating the latest in gunnery, signaling, and fleet tactics ensures the empire's continued command of the seas.

advances.name: Free Trade Dominion
advances.text: The empire's unmatched control of North Sea shipping lanes allows it to dictate the terms of free trade across northern Europe.

advances.name: Parliamentary Union
advances.text: A unified parliament representing England, Denmark, Norway, and the islands formalizes the constitutional basis of the North Sea Empire.

destiny.name: Destiny of the North Sea
destiny.text: The empire that spans three kingdoms and commands the greatest sea in the known world stands at a crossroads. What shall be its destiny?

event.title: A Destiny Takes Shape
event.text:
The North Sea Empire has proven its stability and endurance. What began as an ambitious union of crowns has become a true nation, recognized by its neighbors and feared by its rivals. The foundations are laid. Now the question is what to build upon them.

Our advisors point to the great map in the council chamber, where the blue expanse of our inner sea dominates the center. To the south lie the rich trading cities of Flanders and the Hanse. To the east, the vast forests and rivers where the Varangians once carved kingdoms from the wilderness. The empire's future lies in the direction we choose to march.

destiny.name: Mastery of the Channel
destiny.text: Seize control of the great trading cities of the Low Countries. Bruges and Amsterdam are the keys to northern European commerce. In our hands, they will fund an empire built on trade.

event.title: The Channel Falls Under Our Shadow
event.text:
The great trading cities of the Low Countries, Bruges with its cloth halls and Amsterdam with its warehouses, now fly our banner. The narrowest and busiest stretch of water in northern Europe has become our toll gate. Every bolt of Flemish cloth, every barrel of Rhenish wine, every cargo of Baltic timber that passes through the Channel now enriches our treasury.

The merchants of these cities, once fiercely independent, have discovered that the protection of the North Sea Empire's fleet is worth the price of submission. Our customs officers sit in their counting houses, and our warships patrol the approaches.

options.text: The Channel is our market floor

destiny.name: Hanseatic Subjugation
destiny.text: The Hanseatic League has dominated North Sea trade for too long. Lubeck and Hamburg must bend the knee. Their merchant fleets will serve our crown or be swept from the sea.

event.title: The Fall of the Hanseatic League
event.text:
Lubeck, that proud city that styled itself Queen of the Hanse, has fallen. Hamburg, the gateway to the interior of Germany, flies our colors. The Hanseatic League, for centuries the dominant commercial power of the North Sea and Baltic, has been broken as an independent force.

Their warehouses and counting houses, their ships and their trade routes, their accumulated knowledge of markets from Novgorod to London: all of it now passes into our hands. The question is what to do with this inheritance.

We can absorb their networks quietly, inheriting their merchant contacts and trade intelligence to build our own commercial empire even greater than theirs. Or we can crush them utterly, enforcing our monopoly on North Sea trade with an iron fist and eliminating any future competition.

modifiers.name: Hanseatic Trade Networks
modifiers.text: The absorbed trade intelligence and merchant contacts of the former Hanseatic League fuel our commercial expansion.

modifiers.name: North Sea Monopoly
modifiers.text: Ruthless enforcement of our trade monopoly eliminates competition and bends rival merchants to our will, and every neighbour resents it.

destiny.name: Atlantic Thalassocracy
destiny.text: The ultimate prize: control of the Atlantic approaches. With Rouen and Lisbon in our grasp, no ship sails between the Mediterranean and the Baltic without our leave. The North Sea Empire becomes the arbiter of global trade.

event.title: Lords of the Atlantic
event.text:
With Rouen in Normandy and Lisbon on the Tagus under our control, the North Sea Empire has achieved something unprecedented: dominion over the entire Atlantic seaboard from the Arctic to the Mediterranean approaches. No ship can enter or leave the great ocean without passing through waters we command.

The wealth of the New World, the spice trade, the African gold coast, all the great commercial arteries of the age flow through channels we control. This is the ultimate expression of thalassocratic power.

We can use this position to open the Atlantic to free commerce under our protection, building infrastructure and inviting trade. Or we can assert total control, making every merchant fleet dependent on our goodwill and every naval power subordinate to our admiralty.

options.text: Open the Atlantic to free commerce

modifiers.name: Atlantic Free Commerce
modifiers.text: Open trade policies attract merchants from every corner of the globe, funding massive construction projects across the empire.

options.text: Assert total dominion over all routes

modifiers.name: Atlantic Dominion
modifiers.text: Total control of the Atlantic trade routes allows the empire to integrate distant territories while maintaining a veteran military establishment.

destiny.name: Consolidation of the Realm
destiny.text: Before the empire can expand, it must be unified. Let a Thingstead sit in three towns, hold Nidaros where Saint Olaf lies and the kings of Norway are hailed, and build Copenhagen up from a bishop's harbour town into a royal seat on the Sound, so that each of the three kingdoms answers to one law.

conditions.text: Chose the Crown of Three Kingdoms destiny
A Thingstead stands in at least 3 of our locations
We own Copenhagen and its development is at least 31

event.title: The Realm Consolidated
event.text:
The dream of three kingdoms united under one law has moved from aspiration to reality. The institutions of governance (the shire courts and Thing assemblies, the royal chancellery and the church hierarchy) now function as a single system from the Shetlands to Jutland, from Dublin to Uppsala.

Nidaros keeps the shrine of Saint Olaf under our banner, and Copenhagen has grown from a harbour town into a royal seat on the Sound. Markets operate under uniform regulations, and the king's writ runs unchallenged in every province. The foundation has been laid for something greater: an empire that can project power far beyond its original borders.

options.text: The three kingdoms are truly one

destiny.name: The Eastern March
destiny.text: The Varangians once sailed east to build kingdoms among the Slavs. Now the North Sea Empire shall follow in their wake: take Oreshek at the head of the Neva, Staraya Ladoga where the Norse first settled, and Novgorod itself, and the river road to the east is ours.

event.title: The Eastern March Established
event.text:
Novgorod, the great trading city of the East, has fallen to our armies, and with it Ladoga and the fortress at the head of the Neva. The Varangian dream has been fulfilled at last: the route from Scandinavia to the Byzantine frontier is once again under Norse control. Where Rurik and his companions once came as adventurers, we come as conquerors.

The eastern frontier stretches before us, vast and full of possibility. We can press forward aggressively, using Novgorod as a launching point for further expansion into the Russian heartland. Or we can consolidate this gain, fortifying the eastern frontier and building it into an impregnable bastion that secures our flank while we develop the interior.

modifiers.name: Eastern Offensive
modifiers.text: The momentum of the eastern campaign drives the empire's armies forward at speed, though mercenary costs mount with each new frontier.

modifiers.name: Frontier Bastion
modifiers.text: The eastern frontier is fortified into an impregnable defensive line, securing the empire's flank against all comers.

destiny.name: Imperium of the North
destiny.text: Paris, the jewel of Western Christendom, must acknowledge northern supremacy. With the French capital under our control and London grown to twice its old size, the North Sea Empire becomes the undisputed power of Europe.

conditions.text: We own London and its development is at least 75

event.title: Imperium of the North Proclaimed
event.text:
Paris has fallen. The most prestigious city in Western Christendom, the seat of the Capetian kings, the heart of medieval learning and culture: it is ours. With this conquest, the North Sea Empire has transcended its origins as a maritime union and become the dominant power of the European continent.

The realm now stretches from the Arctic wastes of Greenland to the banks of the Seine, from the forests of Novgorod to the coasts of Ireland. No empire since Rome has commanded such a vast and diverse territory in Europe.

The question of how to govern this colossus admits of two answers. We can rule through overwhelming military force, subjugating all resistance and extracting the wealth of conquered provinces. Or we can seek to harmonize the diverse peoples of the empire, integrating them through law and shared governance into a true universal monarchy.

modifiers.name: Imperial Subjugation
modifiers.text: Conquered provinces are brought to heel through military force, their wealth extracted for the empire's coffers at the cost of noble discontent.

options.text: Harmonize the peoples of the empire

modifiers.name: Harmonized Peoples
modifiers.text: A policy of cultural integration and shared governance binds the empire's diverse peoples together, though the effort of maintaining internal harmony saps the will for prolonged wars.

units.name: Huscarl
units.text: Elite household warriors descended from Cnut's personal guard, the huscarls are fearsome shock troops armed with the great Danish axe. Their devastating charge breaks enemy formations, though their berserker aggression leaves them vulnerable to sustained morale pressure.

units.name: Thingmannalid
units.text: The 'Assembly Men' are the disciplined standing retinue of the North Sea kings. Trained for rapid tactical maneuvers, they strike with initiative and precision, though their lighter armor trades protection for speed.

units.name: Leidang Ship
units.text: A twenty-bench longship furnished, crewed and provisioned by a single ship district for the king's summer fleet. Lighter than a war galley and quick under oar and sail, it carries the district's armed farmers as well as its rowers.

units.name: Knarr
units.text: The broad, deep-hulled trader of the Norse sea roads, built to cross open ocean to Iceland and Greenland under a single square sail. It sails faster and needs fewer hands than a cog, though it carries less.

units.name: Dreki
units.text: The dragon ship, with its carved serpent prow and shallow draft, is the iconic warship of the Norse: fast enough to navigate rivers, seaworthy enough to cross oceans.

units.name: Snekkja
units.text: The 'snake': a nimble, fast-sailing longship ideal for patrol, raiding, and reconnaissance across the empire's vast maritime territory.

units.name: Busse
units.text: A large, heavily-built warship evolved from the merchant knarr, the busse carries significant armament while retaining the seaworthiness of Norse naval design.

units.name: North Sea Frigate
units.text: A purpose-built warship optimized for the rough conditions of the North Sea, combining speed and armament for effective patrol of the empire's vast coastlines.

units.name: Rate-of-the-Line
units.text: A massive ship of the line representing the pinnacle of North Sea naval engineering, bristling with cannon and built to withstand the fiercest Atlantic storms.

units.name: Nordhavskorvet
units.text: A modern corvette designed for the North Atlantic: fast, well-armed, and capable of extended independent operations in the empire's distant waters.

buildings.name: Thingstead
buildings.text: A permanent assembly hall where representatives gather to proclaim laws, settle disputes, and hold rulers accountable in the Norse tradition.

buildings.name: Longship Yards
buildings.text: Specialized shipbuilding facilities using Norse clinker construction, producing the seaworthy vessels that are the sinew of the North Sea Empire.

buildings.name: Herring Hall
buildings.text: The hall of a fishing town, where the catch of the North Sea herring and cod fisheries is landed, salted, barrelled and sold. With a hall to take the catch, the fishery off its coast lands more. The fisheries are the backbone of the empire's maritime commerce.

where.text: The location's raw material is Fish

buildings.name: Danelaw Mint
buildings.text: A royal minting facility producing standardized coinage, the fiscal instrument of the Danegeld taxation system that funds the empire.

buildings.name: Hirdstova
buildings.text: A military training hall where the royal hird, the professional warrior retinue of the Norse kings, hones its skills in arms and tactics.

buildings.name: Stave Church
buildings.text: A distinctively Norse Christian church built from great timber staves, adorned with dragon carvings that blend Christian symbolism with Viking artistry.

buildings.name: Runestone
buildings.text: A carved and painted memorial stone raised beside a road, a bridge or a thing place, naming the dead and the kin who raised it for every passer-by to read.

buildings.name: Admiralty House
buildings.text: The supreme headquarters of the North Sea Empire's naval administration, coordinating the mightiest fleet in the Atlantic world.

buildings.name: Imperial Chancery
buildings.text: The administrative heart of the Imperium of the North, where laws are drafted in three languages and dispatched to every corner of the realm.

list.name: Hird and Witherlogh
list.text: The royal household corps of three to four thousand professional warriors that Cnut retained from his invasion fleet of 1018, governed by the Witherlogh, the Lex Castrensis recorded by Svend Aggesen, blending Norse retainer custom with canon-law procedure. The hird answered to the king alone, bypassing the earls and ealdormen of the shires; Cnut's regulations required each housecarl to bear splendid armour and a gold-hilted double-edged sword.

list.name: Heregeld
list.text: The annual army-tax built on the 1012 ship-tax precedent and famously levied at 72,000 pounds of silver from the shires plus 10,500 from London in 1018, then collected each year until 1051. Assessed on the hide and enforced by forfeit of land to the shire-reeve, the heregeld required precise registers of tenure that anticipated the Domesday survey by half a century.

list.name: Witenagemot
list.text: The Anglo-Saxon council of wise men: archbishops, bishops, abbots, ealdormen, and senior thegns summoned at the king's pleasure to consent to laws and attest grants. Cnut's accession at Oxford in 1018, where Danes and English jointly accepted the laws of Edgar I, was sealed by this body. The Laws of Cnut, drafted by Wulfstan of York between 1020 and 1023, were promulgated through it.

list.name: Wapentake and Riding
list.text: The Danelaw's hundred-courts, where the wapentake (the weapon-taking, confirmation by raised arms) replaced the southern hundred and the riding (thrithjungr, third-part) divided the great northern shires of Yorkshire, Lindsey, and Lincoln. Twelve carucates per small hundred secured the geld assessment, and the sokemen (between thirty and fifty percent of the rural population in eastern England) held intermediate freedoms unknown south of the Thames.

list.name: Skipreiða Leidang
list.text: The Scandinavian coastal levy of ship-districts first attested at the Battle of Hjorungavagr in 985 and reorganised under Haakon the Good. Each skipreide outfitted, crewed, and provisioned a single warship for two to three months. Cnut wove this fleet-conscription together with the Anglo-Saxon ship-soke, the duty of inland shires to fund coastal vessels, giving his federation a unified naval apparatus that drew on both shores of the North Sea.

list.name: Anglo-Danish Mission
list.text: Cnut's instrument for evangelising the Scandinavian half of his empire, anchored on Wulfstan, archbishop of York. From the 1027 Roman pilgrimage onward, English-trained bishops were dispatched to the new northern sees: Bernhard to Skania, Gerbrand to Roskilde, and Ranier to Fyn. The mission was a deliberate counter to Hamburg-Bremen's claims over the Danish church, binding royal authority into the bishoprics from Lund to Trondheim.

list.name: Reformed Coinage
list.text: The late Anglo-Saxon monetary regime of named royal moneyers operating from twelve designated mints, codified by Aethelstan's 928 code and tightened through Edgar's great reform and Aethelred's periodic recoinages. Every penny carried the moneyer's name and mint-place; forced renewals of the silver standard let the Crown skim the seigniorage. Under Cnut the system was extended across the Sound, seeding the first regular silver pennies struck at Lund and Sigtuna.
